stem: Oscar is a 13-year-old boy with asthma who uses a terbutaline (Bricanyl) Turbuhaler when wheezy. Which of the following is the correct sequence of steps for using a Turbuhaler?

options.text: Unscrew the cap, hold the inhaler upright, twist the grip fully one way and back until it clicks, breathe out away from the mouthpiece, seal lips around the mouthpiece, inhale forcefully and deeply, then hold the breath for 10 seconds
Remove the cap, shake the inhaler, exhale into the mouthpiece, press down on the canister while inhaling slowly, then rinse the mouth
Open the cap, load one dose by pressing the base, breathe in gently through the nose, and repeat if symptoms persist
Attach a spacer, breathe out into the spacer, actuate the device, then take several tidal breaths
Prime the inhaler by spraying it into the air, shake well, and inhale through a tight seal at a medium flow

explanation: A Turbuhaler is a dry powder inhaler. The correct technique is to keep it upright, load a dose by twisting the grip until it clicks, breathe out away from the device, then inhale forcefully and deeply through the mouthpiece and hold the breath briefly. It is not shaken, and no spacer is used.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Asthma Management: Medications and Devices - Part A

rationale: This item tests device-specific inhaler technique. Turbuhalers are breath-actuated dry powder inhalers and require a forceful deep inhalation after loading a dose by twisting the grip.

optionExplanations.B: This describes a metered-dose inhaler technique and includes shaking/pressing a canister, which is incorrect for a Turbuhaler.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect: Turbuhalers are not pressed to load and should be inhaled through the mouth, not the nose.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect: spacers are used with pMDIs, not Turbuhalers.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect: Turbuhalers are not primed by spraying into the air and do not require shaking.
